html:
SMTO-BOOT-0041 — SMTO couldn't connect to your model server while starting

GUID: 3b759f80-7245-4e26-97f5-02f325e91f11
Slug: boot-llm-preflight-unreachable
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • While starting, SMTO tried to connect to the server that runs your AI Model and couldn't. SMTO keeps starting, but requests to the Model may fail until it can be reached.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the server that runs your Model is switched on and has finished loading. If it's on another computer, check that computer is on and connected to the network. SMTO only tried to connect, and nothing answered at the address it was given.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing and check the Main model's Endpoint. It must start with http:// or https:// and include the computer name and port. A mistyped or incomplete address makes the connection fail even when the model server is running.
  3. Select Check saved model on that page to confirm the Model actually answers. The startup check only proves something is listening; this button sends the Model a real request.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model reports success, and the next start no longer prints “LLM preflight failed”.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full startup message, including the address it names, and send it to the person who manages SMTO or your model server. A failed connection doesn't prove that work sent to the Model earlier didn't run, so check before repeating it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The optional startup LLM preflight (agent_runtime.api.llm_health) could not parse the configured llm_base_url or open a TCP connection to its host and port; startup continued and no model request was sent.

What this means

  • The startup probe parses the configured model URL and attempts a TCP connection. An invalid URL or failed connection can prevent it from completing. It does not submit a model request, authenticate to the API or test the model; even a successful TCP connection proves only that a listener was reachable.

Why this can happen

  • The configured endpoint may be invalid, or its host and port may not accept a connection from this machine.

How to diagnose it

  • If Technical details report a URL validation failure, correct the configured URL. Otherwise compare the host and port with the provider listener and check reachability from the startup machine.

How to fix it

  • The probe runs from startup.sh when AOR_LLM_PREFLIGHT_ENABLED is on; it resolves the Server's llm_base_url (bootstrap config, environment and saved overrides), requires an http or https URL with a hostname, and attempts a TCP connect within AOR_LLM_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 3). Start or fix the provider listener or correct the URL, rerun python -m agent_runtime.api.llm_health, then confirm real model readiness separately (Settings › Setup › Model routing › Check saved model), because a TCP pass sends no inference.
  • Check the configured model URL and the provider listener, then rerun the startup reachability check. After it passes, verify API and model readiness separately.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The startup probe reports TCP reachability; a separate authorized model request confirms API and model readiness.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • The CLI uses this identity for failed configuration/endpoint results as well as a failed TCP connection; this probe submits no inference.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
